summary: In December 1940, the Bund's newspaper Voice of Youth ran a cover image of two hands shaking through a hole in the ghetto wall with the headline "All men are brothers, whether yellow, black, brown or white."

citation.quote: In December, the Bund's Voice of Youth ran on its cover a picture of two hands shaking through a hole in the ghetto wall. "All men are brothers, whether yellow, black, brown or white," read the headline.

title: Jewish Labor Committee conference at Carnegie Hall
summary: The Jewish Labor Committee held a grand conference at Carnegie Hall to celebrate the rescue of 308 European socialists, with attendees including Friedrich Adler, Raphael Abramovich, Noyakh Portnoy, Julius Deutsch, and Arthur Zygielbojm.

citation.quote: On January 17, 1941, the Jewish Labor Committee threw a grand conference at Carnegie Hall to congratulate themselves on their rescue of European socialists, 308 of whom were in attendance.

title: Sophia Dubnova arrives in Moscow en route to exile
summary: A few weeks after the January 1941 Carnegie Hall conference, Sophia Dubnova, her son Victor, and daughter-in-law Iza disembarked in Moscow on their flight from Europe, visiting the Tretyakov Gallery before continuing east.

citation.quote: A few weeks later, three more of the Jewish Labor Committee's beneficiaries disembarked in Moscow: Sophia Dubnova, her son Victor, and her now daughter-in-law Iza, who had managed to meet up with them in Vilna.

title: Nazis order mass roundups for labor camps
summary: At the end of April 1941, the Nazis ordered mass roundups of ghetto youth for labor camps, with the Jewish Police seizing young people to clear marshes and dig holes under brutal conditions.

citation.quote: At the end of April, the Nazis ordered mass roundups to provide workers for labor camps. At their order, Jewish Police snatched ghetto youth to clear marshes or dig holes in conditions of such lurid sadism that they came back disabled or dead.

title: Gestapo arrests Tsukunft distributor Alter Bas
summary: In early May 1941, the Gestapo arrested Alter Bas, a teenage Tsukunft newspaper distributor, who smuggled out a letter from Pawiak Prison describing how interrogators tore out his fingernails before he expected to perish.

citation.quote: In early May, the Gestapo caught one of the Tsukunft's newspaper distributors, a teenage metalworker named Alter Bas. In a letter that Bas smuggled out of Pawiak Prison, he described how the interrogators had torn out his fingernails.

title: Maurycy Orzech beaten and jailed at Pawiak Prison
summary: After punching a Jewish Policeman who was bludgeoning a woman in the Warsaw ghetto, Maurycy Orzech, head of the Bundist Artisans' Union, was hauled to Pawiak Prison and could not be freed.

citation.quote: One afternoon, Maurycy Orzech, head of the Bundist Artisans' Union, was walking down a ghetto street when he saw a Jewish Policeman bludgeoning a woman. He punched the policeman in the face... until more cops hauled him to Pawiak Prison.

title: Bernard Goldstein flees Gestapo raid; nephew Jacob tortured to death
summary: Tipped off by his janitor, Bernard Goldstein fled his Nowolipie Street apartment minutes before a Gestapo raid; when he failed to surrender, the Gestapo arrested his nephew Jacob and tortured him to death.

citation.quote: Soon afterward, two young Jewish men showed up at Bernard's building at Nowolipie Street and asked the janitor to see the ledger book. They lingered on the letter G... Ten minutes later, Gestapo agents raided his apartment.

title: Celemenski returns to Warsaw ghetto under false identity
summary: In June 1941, Bund courier Jacob Celemenski entered the Warsaw ghetto disguised as a utilities inspector with the Polish name Czeslaw, carrying fake documents from the Polish Socialist Party after months traveling Polish ghettos to organize a canceled Bundist conference.

citation.quote: In June, the Bund's courier Celemenski entered the Warsaw ghetto in the guise of a utilities inspector. He had a new Polish name, Czeslaw, a sharp suit, and several sets of fake documents provided by the Polish Socialist Party.

title: German reconnaissance planes appear over Volkovysk
summary: Avram Markus and other residents of Soviet-occupied Volkovysk began noticing German planes circling overhead, alongside Soviet tanks moving toward the German border.

citation.quote: Around the middle of June, Markus began to notice German planes. They flew in quick circles before they skittered westward.

title: Germany invades the Soviet Union; bombs hit Volkovysk area
summary: German bombers destroyed the Soviet airstrip at Rosh near Volkovysk as Operation Barbarossa began. Molotov announced the Nazi attack and the Red Army began fleeing toward Minsk.

citation.quote: On June 22, explosions interrupted Avram Markus's breakfast. He looked at his wife, Fruma, then out the window. The sounds were coming from Rosh.

title: German incendiary bombs devastate Volkovysk
summary: German bombs hit Broad and Grodno Streets, the Tiferet Bakhurim Synagogue, and the Talmud Torah school in Volkovysk, killing dozens including Joseph Beckenstein.

citation.quote: The next day, German incendiary bombs hit Broad and Grodno Streets, the Tiferet Bakhurim Synagogue, and the Talmud Torah school.

title: Vilna falls to the Nazis
summary: The Lithuanian city of Vilna fell to the advancing Wehrmacht.

citation.quote: Vilna fell on June 23. Minsk on June 24. Riga on June 27.

title: Minsk falls to the Nazis
summary: Minsk was captured by the Wehrmacht during the German invasion of the Soviet Union.

citation.quote: Vilna fell on June 23. Minsk on June 24. Riga on June 27.

title: Kovno falls; Slobodka massacre of Jews
summary: Kovno (Kaunas) fell to the Nazis. Lithuanian partisans stormed the Slobodka suburb, killing the local rabbi and bludgeoning dozens of Jewish men to death.

citation.quote: Kovno fell to the Nazis on June 25. On that day, Lithuanian partisans stormed the rickety-rack Slobodka suburb, tied its famous rabbi to a chair, placed his head on a holy book, and sawed through his neck.

title: Riga falls to the Nazis
summary: Riga fell to the Wehrmacht. Weeks later, the historian Simon Dubnov was shot in the back by a Latvian collaborator while being herded toward the Riga ghetto.

citation.quote: Vilna fell on June 23. Minsk on June 24. Riga on June 27. Sophia's father, the famed historian Simon Dubnov, still lived in Riga.

title: Nazis take Volkovysk
summary: The Nazis captured Volkovysk. German automobiles careened through the streets shooting at random, and yellow stars and race laws followed.

citation.quote: The Nazis took Volkovysk on June 28. In the first days, German automobiles careened through the streets, their passengers shooting out windows at random.

title: Mass killings at Mayak forest, Volkovysk
summary: In the first week of Nazi occupation of Volkovysk, the Mayak forest pits swallowed two hundred people, including the Bundist leader Avram Markus, his wife, and their daughter.

citation.quote: Mayak's pits swallowed two hundred people the first week, including the local Bundist leader Avram Markus, his wife, and their daughter.

title: Sophia Dubnova arrives in Seattle
summary: Sophia Dubnova's ship, the Heian Maru, docked in Seattle. Without U.S. visas, the Erlichs continued on to Vancouver and then Montreal.

citation.quote: Sophia Dubnova's ship, the *Heian Maru,* docked in Seattle in August 1941.

title: Babi Yar massacre
summary: Nazis and Ukrainian collaborators murdered nearly the entire Jewish population of Kyiv, shooting thirty-three thousand naked people at the edge of the Babi Yar ravine.

citation.quote: At the end of September, Nazis and their Ukrainian collaborators murdered almost the entire Jewish population of Kyiv. They lined thirty-three thousand naked humans at the edge of the Babi Yar ravine, then shot them all in the head.

title: Wehrmacht cuts last road to Leningrad
summary: The Wehrmacht severed the last road to Leningrad (formerly Petrograd), beginning the siege of the city.

citation.quote: On September 8, the Wehrmacht cut the last road to Petrograd, which had been renamed again and was now Leningrad. Sophia's beloved city was under siege.

title: Henryk Erlich released from Soviet prison
summary: The NKVD released Henryk Erlich from death row and brought him to Moscow's Hotel Metropole, where Viktor Alter joined him the next day.

citation.quote: The NKVD released Erlich on September 12, 1941, and brought him to Moscow's luxurious Hotel Metropole.

title: Erlich and Alter telegram appears in The Forward
summary: A telegram from Viktor Alter and Henryk Erlich from Moscow's Hotel Metropole appeared in The Forward, signaling their survival and freedom.

citation.quote: This was the state of Soviet defense on September 23, when a telegram appeared in *The Forward.*

title: Wehrmacht reaches Moscow suburbs; Soviet government evacuates
summary: The Wehrmacht reached the suburbs of Moscow. Stalin ordered the government, embassies, and Lenin's corpse evacuated 600 miles east to Kuybyshev (Samara).

citation.quote: In the middle of October, the Wehrmacht reached the suburbs of Moscow. Stalin ordered the government to move six hundred miles east to the old trading city of Kuybyshev, formerly called Samara.

title: Warsaw ghetto marks Bund's 44th anniversary
summary: Two thousand Warsaw ghetto inmates took part in celebrations for the Bund's forty-fourth anniversary. Bund founder Noyakh Portnoy died that same month in New York exile.

citation.quote: In October, two thousand Warsaw ghetto inmates took part in celebrations for the party's forty-fourth anniversary. When one of their founders, Noyakh Portnoy, died that same month in New York exile...

title: Erlich and Alter disappear in Kuybyshev
summary: Just after midnight, Alter was summoned to the telephone at the Grand Hotel in Kuybyshev. He and Erlich left together and never returned, taken by the NKVD.

citation.quote: On December 4, just after midnight, Alter, Erlich, and a friend sat in the Grand Hotel dining room, warming themselves with cups of tea.

title: Shlomo Markus escapes Zhetl ghetto
summary: In spring 1942, Shlomo Markus, the communist son of Bundist editor Avram Markus, escaped the Zhetl ghetto to join the partisans; five months later Germans surrounded his group and he saved his last bullet for himself.

citation.quote: In spring 1942, Shlomo Markus escaped the Zhetl ghetto to join the partisans. Five months later, while he was on a food procurement run in a nearby village, Germans surrounded his group. He saved his last bullet for himself.

title: Five Kravitzes from Lunna Wola arrive at Auschwitz
summary: In 1942, five Kravitzes from Lunna Wola—relatives of Rose, Sam's wife—arrived at Auschwitz via the Kelbasin transit camp and ended up in the gas chambers.

citation.quote: In 1942, five Kravitzes from Lunna Wola arrived at Auschwitz via the Kelbasin transit camp. All of them ended up in the gas chambers.

title: Founding of the Jewish Combat Organization
summary: In 1942, young Zionists in the Warsaw ghetto founded the Jewish Combat Organization.

citation.quote: In 1942, young Zionists in the Warsaw ghetto founded the Jewish Combat Organization.

title: Henryk Erlich kills himself
summary: Four years after his 1938 warning about a Jewish state, Henryk Erlich died by suicide. Those who met him in prison said he remained a Bundist until the end.

citation.quote: Erlich killed himself four years later, as Zionists like to remind me on social media. People who met him in prison say that he remained a Bundist till the end.

title: Grojanowski brings Chelmno gas van report to Warsaw ghetto
summary: Yakov Grojanowski, a Jewish chemist forced by Nazis to bury bodies at Chelmno, brought a report on industrialized murder by poison gas vans to the Warsaw ghetto.

citation.quote: In early February, a Jewish chemist with the pseudonym of Yakov Grojanowski brought an even more shattering report to the ghetto. At a camp in the village of Chelmno, Nazis had applied their German efficiency to the mechanics of mass murder.

title: Arthur Zygielbojm sails to London
summary: Arthur Zygielbojm sailed for London to serve as a Bundist delegate to the Polish government-in-exile, at the suggestion of the Polish Socialist Party.

citation.quote: In March 1942, Arthur Zygielbojm sailed for London to serve as a delegate to the Polish government-in-exile.

title: Meeting of ghetto leftist parties on resistance
summary: Seven delegates from the Warsaw ghetto's leftist parties met at the Bund's Orla Street soup kitchen to discuss resistance. Bundist Maurycy Orzech rejected the call for a united combat group.

citation.quote: On March 23, seven delegates from the ghetto's leftist parties met at the Bund's soup kitchen on Orla Street to discuss resistance. Abrasha Blum and Maurycy Orzech were the Bundist representatives.

title: Gestapo night raid kills Warsaw ghetto activists
summary: Before dawn, the Gestapo invaded the Warsaw ghetto with a list of sixty activists to kill. Guided by the Jewish Police, they pulled activists from their beds and shot them on sidewalks. The Bund lost ten comrades.

citation.quote: Before dawn on April 18, Bernard Goldstein tossed in his narrow bed.

title: Feiner's reports on extermination smuggled to London
summary: A Home Army courier arrived in London carrying two letters from Leon Feiner describing the systematic mass murder of Polish Jews and Roma, demanding Allied action.

citation.quote: At the start of May, a Home Army courier arrived in London, carrying two letters from Leon Feiner, the elegant lawyer who was now the Bund's agent on the Aryan side of Warsaw.

title: German propaganda film made in Warsaw ghetto
summary: German film crews arrived in the Warsaw ghetto to make a propaganda documentary, staging humiliating scenes including forcing well-dressed girls to kick beggars and ordering Hasidim to mime sex with girls.

citation.quote: In May, German film crews arrived to make a documentary about Jewish life in the Warsaw ghetto.

title: Construction begins on Treblinka
summary: Nazis began shipping Poles to a slave labor camp near a small village fifty miles northeast of Warsaw, forcing them to build a facility whose purpose was not explained.

citation.quote: That same month, Nazis started to ship Poles to a slave labor camp near a small village fifty miles northeast of the capital. There, they ordered the Poles to build something. They would not explain its purpose.

title: Henryk Erlich hangs himself in NKVD cell
summary: Bund leader Henryk Erlich, sixty years old and broken by multiple imprisonments, hanged himself from the bars of his Soviet prison cell.

citation.quote: On May 15, 1942, Sophia Dubnova's husband, an intellectual, musically gifted, and affectionate father from Lublin, hung himself from the bars of his cell.

title: Adam Czerniakow commits suicide
summary: Unable to endure the deportation of the ghetto's children, Judenrat chairman Adam Czerniakow swallowed cyanide on the second day of the Great Aktion.

citation.quote: Unable to endure the upcoming deportation of the ghetto's children, Judenrat chairman Adam Czerniakow had swallowed cyanide.

title: Nazis offer bread bribe for voluntary deportation
summary: In late July, Nazis enticed starving ghetto inmates with three kilograms of bread and one kilogram of marmalade to volunteer for deportation, drawing in even the Bund's strongest fighters.

citation.quote: In late July, Nazis offered the starving ghetto inmates an enticement. Anyone who volunteered for deportation would get three kilograms of bread and one kilogram of marmalade.

title: New York Times prints Bund's extermination report
summary: The New York Times printed a small item on the Bund's report of the final solution, after Zygielbojm publicized it via the British government, The Telegraph, and the BBC.

citation.quote: On July 2, *The New York Times* printed a small item, of the sort it now runs about similar far-flung genocides. Thanks to the Bund, Americans read about the final solution at their breakfast tables.

title: Deportation order posted in Warsaw ghetto on Tisha b'Av
summary: On Tisha b'Av, German posters appeared throughout the Warsaw ghetto announcing the deportation of all Jews regardless of age or sex, with death the penalty for non-compliance.

citation.quote: July 22 was Tisha b'Av, the day when Jews mourn the destruction of the temple in Jerusalem. A young Bundist named Vladka Peltel was in her mother's home when her neighbor burst in to tell them about the posters.

title: Nazis begin liquidating the Warsaw ghetto
summary: The Great Aktion began as German forces and their helpers started mass deportations from the Warsaw ghetto, packing thousands of Jews onto boxcars bound for Treblinka.

citation.quote: It was drizzling on July 22, 1942, when the Nazis began to liquidate the Warsaw ghetto.

title: Sonia Nowogrodska seized for the Umschlagplatz
summary: While waiting for Maurycy Orzech's phone call about a weapons heist, Marek Edelman watched from the window as Nazis drove Sonia Nowogrodska toward the Umschlagplatz.

citation.quote: He told Marek to wait for his call at Sonia Nowogrodska's old apartment, one of the only places in the ghetto with a working phone line. He would call the morning of August 13.

title: The Cauldron selection in the Warsaw ghetto
summary: Six weeks after deportations began, Germans forced the last hundred thousand ghetto Jews into a single block for a two-day selection nicknamed 'the cauldron,' in which only those given numbered slips were spared.

citation.quote: On September 6, six weeks after they started their deportations, the Germans forced the last hundred thousand ghetto Jews into a single block for a two-day selection that prisoners nicknamed "the cauldron."

title: Mass deportations from Warsaw ghetto end
summary: The Great Aktion ended after taking most of Warsaw's Bundists. That night was Yom Kippur, exactly forty-five years since the Bund's creation, and the Bund published a newspaper with Zalman Friedrich's Treblinka report.

citation.quote: The mass deportations ended on September 21, 1942. They had taken most of Warsaw's Bundists with them.

title: The Erlichs arrive in New York
summary: After nearly circumnavigating the globe over three years from Warsaw, the Erlichs disembarked at Pennsylvania Station, where Viktor Alter's sister Esther Iwinska met them.

citation.quote: In October 1942, the Erlichs disembarked at New York City's Pennsylvania Station. In the three years since they set out from Warsaw, they had nearly circumnavigated the globe.

title: Bund joins the Jewish Combat Organization (ZOB)
summary: After the deciding vote by Tsukunft leader Henoch Russ, the Bund joined the ZOB with Marek Edelman as their commander, creating a coordinating committee with the Zionists.

citation.quote: In late October, the Bund joined the ZOB, with Marek Edelman as their commander.

title: Jan Karski meets Feiner and Berman
summary: Home Army courier Jan Karski met Bundist Leon Feiner and Zionist Adolf Berman in a ruined villa near Warsaw. Feiner gave him a report on the Nazi extermination campaign that had consumed over 1.2 million lives.

citation.quote: That October, Home Army courier Jan Karski met two Jewish leaders in a ruined villa on the outskirts of Warsaw. One was the Zionist Adolf Berman, and the other was the Bundist Leon Feiner.

title: Home Army gives ZOB ten revolvers
summary: The Polish Home Army finally provided the Jewish Combat Organization with ten revolvers, refusing further weapons because General Rowecki did not believe Jews would use them.

citation.quote: In December the Home Army finally gave the ZOB ten revolvers. Despite the ZOB's pleas, no more guns arrived. Rowecki didn't believe that Jews would use them.

title: Karski meets Arthur Zygielbojm in London
summary: Jan Karski met Bund delegate Arthur Zygielbojm at Stratton House in London, delivering Leon Feiner's report on the Holocaust and conveying the Warsaw Bundists' demands to the world.

citation.quote: The Polish Home Army courier Jan Karski arrived in London in November, with a microfilm copy of Feiner's report hidden inside his hollowed-out fake teeth. On December 2, Karski met Arthur Zygielbojm at the bustling Stratton House, where the Polish Ministry of the Interior was headquartered.

title: Gina Klepfisz buried at Brodno cemetery
summary: After dying from infection following ulcer surgery in a Catholic hospital, the Bundist nurse Gina Klepfisz was buried by Bundists and Polish socialists under her Polish pseudonym Kazimiera Juzwiak.

citation.quote: On December 5, comrades buried Gina at the Catholic Brodno cemetery, with her Polish pseudonym engraved on the tombstone.

title: Shaindel Kirsch sent to Blizyn camp
summary: After the Germans killed her family, Bundist Shaindel Kirsch was shipped to Blizyn concentration camp to work as a sewing slave, later receiving a coded message that funded her escape.

citation.quote: In 1943, they shipped her to Blizyn concentration camp to work as a sewing slave. One autumn day, a trash man sidled up and told her to wait that night by the barbed wire fence for a secret message.

title: January revolt in the Warsaw ghetto
summary: Jewish fighters, including Mordechai Anielewicz, surprised German troops during a deportation action, sparking three days of clashes that proved armed defiance was possible.

citation.quote: For the next three days, clashes raged around the ghetto. In the Schutz factory, Bundist Avram Feiner died trying to grab a German's carbine. Germans caught Boruch Peltz's Bundist battle squad unarmed and herded them to the Umschlagplatz.

title: Death of Halinka Kipman
summary: Fourteen-year-old Halinka Kipman was killed during the January revolt in the Warsaw ghetto, her body found by Janina Bauman beside that of her boyfriend.

citation.quote: Of all January's victims, I think first of a fourteen-year-old girl named Halinka Kipman, whose name I found in journalist Janina Bauman's youthful ghetto memoir Winter in the Morning.

title: Gestapo captures Michal Klepfisz
summary: The Gestapo arrested Bundist engineer and bomb-maker Michal Klepfisz and put him on a boxcar to Treblinka; he sawed through the window bars and jumped from the moving train, wounded by a guard's bullet.

citation.quote: The Gestapo caught Michal Klepfisz at the end of January and put him on a boxcar to Treblinka. He took a file hidden beneath his clothes and sawed through the window bars, then pulled himself through and jumped from the moving train. A guard shot him in the ankle as he ran.

title: First armed Jewish resistance in Warsaw ghetto
summary: Nazis entered the ghetto for a new round of roundups, taking the ZOB by surprise. Mordechai Anielewicz's Hashomer Hatzair fighters infiltrated a deportation column, and seventeen-year-old Margalit Landau threw the first grenade at Mila and Zamenhof.

citation.quote: On January 18, 1943, just before sunrise, Nazis entered the ghetto for a new round of roundups. They banged doors, demanding Jews come out.

title: Planned ZOB demonstration in Muranow Square
summary: The ZOB had planned a public demonstration to take over streets, hang wreathes for the fallen, light a bonfire in Muranow Square, and arrest Jewish Policemen, but the January 18 Nazi raid preempted it.

citation.quote: On January 21, fighters would take over several streets in the central ghetto, hang wreathes and banners to commemorate the fallen, and light a bonfire in Muranow Square.

title: Soviets retake Stalingrad
summary: After six months of combat, the Red Army recaptured the ruins of Stalingrad at the cost of a million lives, dealing the first major blow to Nazi invincibility.

citation.quote: After six months of combat, the Red Army had turned the destroyed city into a death trap for the German invaders. At the start of February, the Soviets retook the ruins, at the cost of a million lives.

title: NKVD shoots Viktor Alter
summary: After being held in solitary confinement in the Kuybyshev prison without charges, Bund leader Viktor Alter was shot by the NKVD a week before Litvinov's letter disclosing his death.

citation.quote: The NKVD shot Viktor Alter in February 1943, a week before Litvinov's letter. After his death, they burned his possessions.

title: Litvinov reveals Alter and Erlich executions
summary: Soviet ambassador Maxim Litvinov informed AFL chairman William Green by letter that Bund leaders Henryk Erlich and Viktor Alter had been shot as Nazi collaborators the previous December.

citation.quote: In a letter dated February 23, 1943, he informed Green that the two leaders had been shot as Nazi collaborators that past December.

title: Toebbens deportation ruse fails
summary: The Nazis appointed German industrialist Walter Toebbens to lure remaining ghetto workers onto boxcars with promises of a labor camp; a ZOB poster campaign ensured no one believed him.

citation.quote: In March, they appointed the German industrialist Walter Toebbens to convince the ghetto's forty thousand remaining workers to voluntarily load themselves onto the boxcars.

title: Warsaw ghetto uprising begins
summary: In the first hours of April 19, thousands of German troops massed for the long-awaited liquidation; ZOB and ZZW fighters mobilized and ambushed the Nazi convoy with Molotov cocktails, repelling them by afternoon.

citation.quote: When operatives on the Aryan side called the ZOB central command in the first hours of April 19 to say that thousands of men were massing outside the ghetto walls for the long-awaited liquidation, they were ready.

title: Samsonowicz's appeal to Warsaw's Poles
summary: Bundist writer Ignacy Samsonowicz issued an appeal in the name of the ZOB to Warsaw's Polish population, calling for solidarity in the fight against the Nazi invader.

citation.quote: On April 23, the Bundist writer Ignacy Samsonowicz appealed to Warsaw's Polish population in the name of the Jewish Combat Organization.

title: Sikorski telegram warns against wider revolt
summary: Prime Minister Sikorski telegrammed Home Army commander Rowecki that aiding Jews was acceptable but the uprising must not be allowed to spread to Aryan Warsaw.

citation.quote: Prime Minister Sikorski said as much to Rowecki in an April 27 telegram. It was fine to aid Jews, but the uprising must not be allowed to spread to Aryan Warsaw.

title: Bundist fighters sing the Internationale
summary: On May Day, surviving Bundist fighters in the burning Warsaw ghetto buried their dead and lined up to sing The Internationale as Germans pumped chlorine gas into their bunkers.

citation.quote: On May Day, the Bundist fighters buried their dead, then lined up to sing "The Internationale."

title: Fall of Mila 18 bunker
summary: Bloodhounds discovered the ZOB's command post at 18 Mila Street; trapped by chlorine gas, commander Mordechai Anielewicz shot his beloved Mira Fuchrer and then himself alongside many of the 120 fighters inside.

citation.quote: On May 8, bloodhounds discovered the ZOB's command post at 18 Mila Street. It was a vast bunker, owned by a mob boss named Shmuel Asher, supplied with power, water, even vodka from the Aryan side.

title: Zygielbojm hears of ghetto's final destruction
summary: Bundist representative Arthur Zygielbojm listened to the Polish underground radio declare the murders of the last Jews in the Warsaw ghetto, guessing his wife and son were among them.

citation.quote: On May 11, Zygielbojm listened to the Polish underground radio declare the murders of the last Jews in the Warsaw ghetto. He probably guessed his wife and his son were among them.

title: Suicide of Arthur Zygielbojm
summary: In his Paddington apartment, Bundist representative Arthur Zygielbojm swallowed poison in protest against the world's inactivity, leaving letters to Sikorski, his brother, and his New York comrades.

citation.quote: The next night, in his Paddington apartment, he swallowed poison. Before he did, he wrote three letters.

title: Stroop declares Warsaw ghetto liquidation complete
summary: SS commander Jurgen Stroop announced the liquidation of the Warsaw ghetto complete and ordered the Great Synagogue on Tlomackie Street dynamited to celebrate.

citation.quote: On May 16, Stroop declared the liquidation of the Warsaw ghetto complete. To celebrate, he ordered his men to dynamite the Great Synagogue on Tlomackie Street.

title: Gestapo captures General Stefan Rowecki
summary: The Gestapo captured the Home Army's General Stefan Rowecki, who was replaced by the aristocratic Bronislaw Bor-Komorowski, who refused to aid Jewish partisans.

citation.quote: At the end of June, the Gestapo captured the Home Army's General Stefan Rowecki. For all his flaws, Rowecki was competent and fair-minded, and he armed the ghetto fighters in the end.

title: Sikorski's plane crashes; Knoll memo on Jews
summary: After Prime Minister Sikorski's plane crashed returning from the Middle East, the government-in-exile lurched further right; that July, Endek politician Roman Knoll wrote a memo opposing Jewish return to Poland.

citation.quote: Shortly after Rowecki's arrest, Prime Minister Sikorski's plane crashed on his way back from the Middle East. After Sikorski's death, the government-in-exile lurched further to the right. Indicative of this shift is a memo, written that July by Endek politician Roman Knoll, the director of foreign affairs.

title: Bor-Komorowski orders execution of Jewish partisans
summary: Home Army commander Bor-Komorowski ordered his commanders to execute Jewish partisans on sight, regarding them as commie criminals.

citation.quote: To the good general, Jewish partisans were merely commie criminals. In September, he ordered his commanders to execute them on sight.

title: Bundists send greetings to Swiss Social Democrats
summary: Bundists used an illegal radio in September to send greetings from their Warsaw safe house to the Swiss Social Democratic Party's annual congress.

citation.quote: In September, they used an illegal radio to send greetings from their Warsaw safe house to the Swiss Social Democratic Party's annual congress.

title: Leon Feiner's report to the government-in-exile
summary: Leon Feiner wrote a November report describing Bundist efforts to keep alive the remnants of Polish Jewry hidden in Aryan Warsaw.

citation.quote: "Our tasks now come down to this: to keep alive the remnants who have survived…so there will be some reserve for the future and witnesses to this crime," wrote Leon Feiner in his November report to the government-in-exile.

title: National Armed Forces join the Home Army
summary: Bor-Komorowski welcomed the Nazi-collaborationist paramilitary National Armed Forces into the Home Army.

citation.quote: The next March, Bor-Komorowski welcomed a Nazi-collaborationist paramilitary called the National Armed Forces into the Home Army.

title: Red Army liberates Volkovysk
summary: After the largest tank battle in history at Kursk, the Soviets rolled through Ukraine and into Poland, with the Red Army liberating Volkovysk in July 1944.

citation.quote: After the largest tank battle in history, at Kursk, the Soviets rolled through Ukraine and into Poland. The Red Army liberated Volkovysk in July 1944.

title: Soviets set up provisional government in Lublin
summary: At the end of July, the Soviets set up a provisional government in Lublin which included Polish socialists and three Bundists: Leo Finkelstein, Grisza Jaszunski, and Michael Schuldenfrei.

citation.quote: At the end of July, the Soviets set up a provisional government in Lublin, which included Polish socialists and three Bundists: Leo Finkelstein, Grisza Jaszunski, and Michael Schuldenfrei.

title: Red Army tanks enter Praga; Warsaw Uprising begins
summary: On July 31, Red Army tanks entered Praga; the Bund's central committee meeting was interrupted by news that the Warsaw uprising had begun.

citation.quote: On July 31, Red Army tanks entered Praga. The Bund's central committee met at Ignacy Samsonowicz's apartment to discuss the Soviet arrival. The meeting had barely started when Samsonowicz's lover burst in with news from her Home Army friends. The Warsaw uprising had begun.

title: Liberation of Paris
summary: Paris was liberated in August 1944 by Free French forces; de Gaulle shipped Black African soldiers home before reaching the capital to maintain the appearance of French self-liberation.

citation.quote: Paris was liberated in August 1944. The men who had fought their way through the South of France were largely colonial troops—Senegalese, Maghrebi, or Martinican, like the young Frantz Fanon—but this would not do for Free French commander Charles de Gaulle's self-image.

title: Gershon Beckenstein recorded in Buchenwald archives
summary: Gershon Beckenstein, a Volkovysk relative who played in the Auschwitz orchestra, appears in the Buchenwald archives in January 1945; Buchenwald rebelled that April.

citation.quote: A cellblock friend testified that Gershon died just before the camp's evacuation, but the musician's name appears in the Buchenwald archives, in January 1945. Buchenwald rebelled that April.

title: Polish underground leader Jerzy Braun on Jewish returnees
summary: Polish underground leader Jerzy Braun declared there was no place for Jews in Polish towns and countryside, framing antisemitism as economic law as returning Jewish survivors faced hostility and violence.

citation.quote: "There is no place for a Jew in the countryside and towns today," since Poles had taken over their businesses, said the Polish underground leader Jerzy Braun in July 1945.

title: Jacob Pat returns to Poland to distribute Jewish Labor Committee aid
summary: Bundist Jacob Pat returned to Poland in 1946 to distribute aid for the Jewish Labor Committee, finding only twenty-three Bund members left in his hometown of Bialystok where the party had once won fifteen thousand votes.

citation.quote: The Bundist Jacob Pat realized the same when he returned to Poland in 1946 to distribute aid for the Jewish Labor Committee. In his hometown, Bialystok, where the Bund won fifteen thousand votes in the prewar municipal elections, the party had only twenty-three members left.

title: Barbed wire comes down at DP camps
summary: At the request of Jewish groups, Americans took down the barbed wire around the first DP camps and allowed Jews to live in separate camps away from Nazi collaborators, though conditions remained grim.

citation.quote: The barbed wire that circled the first camps came down in 1946. At the request of Jewish groups, Americans allowed Jews to live in separate camps, away from the Nazi collaborators.

title: Bundist conference at Feldafing DP camp
summary: 150 Bundists who had been dispersed across Germany gathered in the Feldafing DP camp in Bavaria for a three-day conference and decided to run for survivors' committees that constituted camp self-governance.

citation.quote: On June 1, 1946, 150 of those Bundists who had been "dispersed and shoved aside all over Germany" gathered in the Feldafing DP camp in Bavaria for a three-day conference to figure out what came next.

title: Kielce pogrom
summary: After a Polish boy blamed Jews for kidnapping him, Polish mobs, joined by cops and soldiers, slaughtered forty-two young Jewish residents in the southeastern city of Kielce.

citation.quote: The final blow fell in July 1946, in the southeastern city of Kielce, when a Polish boy came home late. He blamed the Jews, as one did, saying that they had locked him in the basement of a communal apartment building, where they planned to make matzoh from his blood... Polish mobs slaughtered forty-two young Jewish residents. Cops and soldiers joined in.

title: UN approves partition plan for Palestine
summary: At the end of 1947, the United Nations approved a partition plan for Palestine, granting Jews 56 percent of the land despite being only a third of the population. Palestinian leadership rejected the offer.

citation.quote: At the end of 1947, the United Nations approved a partition plan for Palestine, which granted Jews, who were a only a third of the population, 56 percent of the land. Palestinian leadership understandably rejected this offer.

title: Bund reconstitutes as international organization in New York
summary: In 1947, the Bund reconstituted itself as an international organization with its base in New York City. At their first conference they called for a secular, democratic Palestine and said Zionists must renounce the goal of an independent Jewish state.

citation.quote: That year, the Bund reconstituted itself as an international organization, with its base now in New York City. At their first conference they called for a secular, democratic Palestine, with cultural autonomy and constitutionally protected equal rights, and said that Zionists must "renounce the goal of an independent Jewish state."

title: Bund's fiftieth anniversary celebrations
summary: On the Bund's fiftieth anniversary, the party's flag went up in German DP camps, a Shanghai social club, and a Roman union hall. In New York's Manhattan Center, five thousand people watched Vladka Peltel hand the banner to seventy-eight-year-old John Mill.

citation.quote: In November 1947, the Bund's flag went up in German DP camps, in a Shanghai social club, and at a Roman union hall. It was their fiftieth anniversary. In New York's Manhattan Center, five thousand people watched the young courier Vladka Peltel hand the party's banner to seventy-eight-year-old John Mill, the last surviving Bundist pioneer.

title: Antek Zuckerman joins his wife in Palestine
summary: Antek Zuckerman, founder of the Jewish Combat Organization, joined his wife Celina in Palestine in 1948, where they spent the rest of their lives on a kibbutz for ghetto fighters built on the ruins of a Palestinian village.

citation.quote: Antek's wife, Celina, had already left for Palestine, where she gave birth to their child. He joined her there in 1948. The two heroes of the uprising spent the rest of their lives on a kibbutz for ghetto fighters like them, built on the ruins of a Palestinian village, ethnically cleansed by Zionist militias that became the IDF.

title: Death of Shloyme Mendelson
summary: In his last article written before his death in 1948, Bernard Goldstein's best friend Shloyme Mendelson condemned the totalitarian methods Zionism used to repress Jewish dissent.

citation.quote: In his last article written before his death in 1948, Bernard Goldstein's best friend Shloyme Mendelson condemned the "totalitarian" methods that Zionism used to repress Jewish dissent.

title: Congress passes restrictive Displaced Persons bill
summary: When Congress finally passed the bill to accept survivors in 1948, it banned 90 percent of Jewish survivors because they had taken wartime refuge in the Soviet Union.

citation.quote: When the bill finally passed in 1948, it banned 90 percent of Jewish survivors, because they had taken wartime refuge in the Soviet Union.

title: Ben-Gurion approves draft for Jewish refugees in Europe
summary: In March 1948, David Ben-Gurion approved a draft for Jewish refugees in Europe to fight for the Haganah, claiming them as Israeli citizens despite Israel not yet existing.

citation.quote: In March 1948, David Ben-Gurion approved a draft for Jewish refugees in Europe. They were not Israeli citizens, as Israel didn't exist, nor were they all Zionists. The Haganah claimed them as fighters merely because they were Jews

title: Congress of Survivors resolves against draft dodgers
summary: On March 30, the Congress of Survivors in the American occupation zone of Germany resolved that draft dodgers would be removed from all social and political life, leading to firings, fines, and blacklists targeting Bundists.

citation.quote: When appeals to patriotism failed, Zionists turned to stronger inducements. On March 30, the Congress of Survivors in the American occupation zone of Germany resolved that "draft dodgers" would be "removed from all social and political life."

title: Ethnic cleansing of Haifa
summary: On the eve of Passover 1948, exactly five years after the Warsaw ghetto revolt, Zionist paramilitaries ethnically cleansed fifteen thousand Palestinians from Haifa.

citation.quote: Exactly five years after the ghetto revolt, on the eve of Passover 1948, Zionist paramilitaries ethnically cleansed fifteen thousand Palestinians from Haifa.

title: Ben-Gurion declares the State of Israel
summary: Ben-Gurion announced the state of Israel in May 1948 with the support of the Soviet Union and the United States. In the attacks before and during the war that followed, Zionist militias violently expelled over 750,000 Palestinians from their homes.

citation.quote: Ben-Gurion announced the state of Israel in May 1948, with the support of the Soviet Union and the United States. In the attacks that preceded the declaration, and in the war that followed, Zionist militias violently expelled over 750,000 Palestinians from their homes.

title: Bund Bulletin condemns Israel's refusal to allow Palestinian return
summary: In the Bulletin of September 1948, the Bund condemned Israel for forfeiting the moral rights of Jewish DPs by refusing to permit Arab refugees to return to their homes in Palestine.

citation.quote: "True to its Zionist self, the Jewish Government of the State of Israel appears ready to forfeit the moral rights of the Jewish DPs in Europe and elsewhere by refusing to permit the Arab refugees to return to their homes in Palestine."

title: W.E.B. Du Bois visits the Warsaw ghetto ruins
summary: Du Bois visited the ruins of the Warsaw ghetto and described the fighters' deliberate sacrifice as something that reinforced his commitment to universalist socialism.

citation.quote: When W.E.B. Du Bois visited the ghetto's ruins in 1949, he described the fighters' "deliberate sacrifice in life for a great ideal in the face of the fact that the sacrifice might be completely in vain" as something that reinforced his commitment to universalist socialism.

title: Polish Bund votes to dissolve itself
summary: Under extreme pressure from the Soviet-backed government, which had forced the Polish Socialist Party to merge with the communists, the Polish Bund voted to dissolve itself in 1949.

citation.quote: The Bund was next. Under extreme pressure, the party voted to dissolve itself in 1949. Some members disappeared into private life. Others, including most of Tsukunft's leadership, smuggled themselves out of Poland.

title: DP camp conscription ends
summary: Conscription of Jewish DPs continued until April 1949, at which point recruits from DP camps made up a third of the new Israeli army.

citation.quote: Conscription continued until April 1949, at which point recruits from DP camps made up a third of the new Israeli army.

title: Bund Bulletin on Arab refugee crisis
summary: The Bund wrote in the Bulletin in June 1949 about more than half a million Arab displaced persons demanding permission to return to their former homes.

citation.quote: "At present, when more than half a million Arab displaced persons are demanding permission to return to their former homes...how the State of Israel could cope with a Jewish immigration of any scope without the 'miracle' of the vanished Arabs is beyond anybody's imagination. Yet the Arab refugee problem remains most urgent," wrote the Bund in the Bulletin in June 1949.

title: Bund reduced to scattered Holocaust survivor communities
summary: By 1950 the once-mighty Bund had been reduced to small communities of Holocaust survivors scattered across the globe, who turned to each other and moved into the same apartment buildings and factory jobs.

citation.quote: By 1950, the once mighty movement had been reduced to small communities of Holocaust survivors scattered across the globe. Exhausted, traumatized, and with most of their loved ones dead, these Bundists turned to each other.

title: Bund Bulletin reports on Palestinian refugee camps
summary: In 1951, the Bund Bulletin ran a story about the hundreds of thousands of Palestinian refugees in camps in neighboring countries, prevented from returning home and with property confiscated.

citation.quote: In 1951, the Bund Bulletin ran a story about the hundreds of thousands of Palestinian refugees in camps in neighboring countries, "prevented from returning to their homesteads and villages and whose property is as good as confiscated by the conqueror."

title: The Bund in Pictures published
summary: A photographic history of the Bund, The Bund in Pictures, bound in smoke-blue cloth and resembling a high school yearbook, was published in 1957.

citation.quote: For this reason, one of my prized possessions is a photographic history of the Bund, The Bund in Pictures, published in 1957.

title: Death of Bernard Goldstein
summary: Bundist leader Bernard Goldstein died and was buried in Mount Carmel Cemetery in Queens on the honor walk of Yiddish socialists, near his onetime cellmate Vladimir Medem.

citation.quote: Bernard Goldstein died in 1959. He is buried in Mount Carmel Cemetery in Queens, on the honor walk of Yiddish socialists, not far from his onetime cellmate Vladimir Medem.

title: Murder of Lawrence Rothbort
summary: Sam Rothbort's son Lawrence, described as brilliant and tormented, was murdered in 1963.

citation.quote: He made art with his son, the brilliant, tormented Lawrence, who was murdered in 1963.

title: Death of Alexander Kerensky in New York
summary: After fleeing Petrograd in 1917, Alexander Kerensky settled in New York City, where he lived until his death in 1970, visiting the Bund's archives to research material for his diatribes against Lenin.

citation.quote: After Kerensky fled Petrograd in a car flying the American flag, he'd followed the path of so many political exiles, to New York City, where he settled until his death in 1970.

title: Irving Howe letter on Bundist confronting Said at Columbia
summary: In a 1978 letter, writer Irving Howe complained about an incident at Columbia University, where after debating Edward Said about Israel, a little old Bundist attacked Zionists and Israelis from the audience.

citation.quote: In one letter I found, from 1978, the writer Irving Howe complained about an incident at Columbia University, where he debated Edward Said about Israel. When it came time for questions, a little old Bundist with a thick Yiddish accent sprang up.

title: Najla Said meets Alexander Erlich wearing Solidarity pin
summary: In 1981, seven-year-old Najla Said and her father Edward Said ran into Alexander Erlich in front of his building. Erlich wore a pin for Solidarity, the Polish trade-union movement, prompting her father to explain what solidarity meant.

citation.quote: Over email, Said's daughter, Najla, recalled a moment in 1981, when she was only seven. She and her father ran into Erlich in front of his building. Erlich wore a pin for Solidarity, the Polish trade-union movement that would help bring down the country's dictatorship.

title: Death of Sophia Dubnova
summary: Sophia Dubnova died at age 101 in New York, lucid to the last. Shortly before her death she told her grandson Henry she was no longer a socialist but an anarchist.

citation.quote: She died in 1986, at age 101, engaged and lucid to the last. Shortly before her death, she told her grandson Henry she had a confession to make. She was no longer a socialist but an anarchist.

title: Solidarity movement leads to end of Polish dictatorship

title: Collapse of the Soviet Union opens NKVD files
summary: The collapse of the Soviet Union eventually allowed the release of NKVD files that had entombed the true story of Henryk Erlich's fate.

title: Author covers Occupy Wall Street protests

title: Author publishes Bund article in NYRB

title: Bundist ideas circulate after New York Review of Books article

title: Melbourne swastika covered by Bund sticker
